newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mediterranean-based prices dominate India diesel.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean-based prices dominate India diesel.

text.p: Lower diesel prices in the Mediterranean compared with Asia, once again spurred sellers to make most of their offers into India's tender for May arrival cargoes based on Mediterranean prices, traders said on Thursday.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has awarded in two tenders for April arrival cargoes based on Mediterranean spot quotes.

The spread between Asia and the Mediterranean for physical cargoes has widened to $45 per tonne, $10 more than a month ago, while the physical East/West spread (Asia/Europe) is about $36.00 per tonne.
The forward April East/West spread is about $25.00 per tonne.

The offers in the current tender were made around the same levels as in the previous one, with cargoes to the Indian east coast seen between $28.00 and $30.00 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
Cargoes for delivery to the Indian west coast were seen between $24.00 and $28.50 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f basis.
A MidEast refiner was said to have made an aggressive offer of 50 cents per barrel above MidEast quotes on a free-on board (fob) basis.
IOC is expected to take about 500,000 tonnes in this tender, which closed on March 20 which is expected to be awarded later this evening.
India bought 600,000 tonnes in 14 cargoes for delivery last May.
But some traders said this time IOC might take as much as 700,000-800,000 tonnes.
However they noted that IOC has recently started to issue supplementary tenders over their first tender for March and April delivery and might do the same again this time.
They said by doing this, IOC has managed to curb any drastic price spike if it met market anticipation by buying large volumes in one tender.
For example, in its tender for April arrival, IOC was expected to take as much as 700,000 tonnes in one tender.
Instead, it took 570,000 tonnes in the first tender and issued a second tender when it took another 120,000-135,000 tonnes.
"By taking supplementary cargoes in a second tender, they managed to get much lower prices," one trader said. "It's to their benefit to do that."

For example, British Petroleum sold them one cargo at a very low price of $20.48 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, c-and-f west coast, which was about $5.00 below the lowest priced cargo in the first tender.
IOC took 615,000 tonnes of diesel in its first tender for March arrival and an additional 80,000-90,000 tonnes in a supplementary tender.
